The following sentence was added to the end of Inclusion Criterion 5:

"Subjects with a history of herpes zoster must have completed any required antiviral treatment at least 30 days prior to Day 1."

This change was made to clarify the required washout period for subjects with a history of herpes zoster, and to align with the most recent FDA and EMA guidance on live-attenuated vaccine washout periods. The change does not affect the study population or the safety profile of the study.

The protocol amendment cover letter states Trial Protocol LUM-301 amendment_effective_date is 2025-09-01. Record status: current. This version is the current effective version of the protocol and supersedes all previous versions.

**2. SUMMARY OF CHANGES**

The following table provides a summary of the substantive changes made in this amendment. Section numbers refer to the numbering in the previous version (3.1) of the protocol.

| Section | Description of Change | Rationale |
|---------|------------------------|-----------|
| 5.3 | Clarified that subjects who complete the 24-week treatment period and enter the 52-week follow-up period will be assessed for nasal polyp score at each visit, regardless of whether they have received rescue therapy. | To ensure consistency in the collection of efficacy data during the follow-up period. |
| 7.2 | Added a new subsection 7.2.4 describing the procedures for unscheduled safety visits, including the requirement to perform a serum pregnancy test for female subjects of childbearing potential. | To provide clarity on the conduct of unscheduled visits and to align with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines. |
| 9.1 | Updated the list of permitted concomitant medications to include short courses of systemic corticosteroids (up to 5 days) for the treatment of acute exacerbations of CRSwNP, with a washout period of 14 days before any scheduled efficacy assessment. | To reflect the clinical reality that subjects may require rescue therapy for acute exacerbations, while ensuring that such therapy does not confound the efficacy analysis. |
| 11.3 | Revised the statistical analysis plan for the primary endpoint (change from baseline in total nasal polyp score at Week 24) to specify the use of a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) as the primary analysis method, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. | To align with the most recent regulatory guidance on the analysis of continuous endpoints in confirmatory trials. |
| 13.6 | Expanded the adverse event reporting period to include all serious adverse events (SAEs) occurring within 30 days of the last dose of study drug, rather than the previous 14-day period. | To comply with updated safety reporting requirements from the Health Sciences Authority (HSA). |
| 15.2 | Clarified that subjects who discontinue study drug early will be encouraged to remain in the study for follow-up visits, and that every effort will be made to obtain a final safety assessment at the end of the follow-up period. | To minimise missing data and to ensure the completeness of the safety database. |

**3. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF CHANGES**

**3.1 Section 5.3 – Follow-up Period**

The following text has been added to the end of Section 5.3:

"Subjects who complete the 24-week treatment period will enter a 52-week follow-up period. During this period, subjects will be assessed for nasal polyp score at each visit, regardless of whether they have received rescue therapy for acute exacerbations of CRSwNP. If a subject undergoes nasal polyp surgery during the follow-up period, the nasal polyp score will be recorded as the baseline value for the purpose of subsequent analyses."

The current ethical approval for LUM-301, granted under GHEB reference number GHEB/2024/LUM-301/APR-07, expired on 30 November 2025. The Board notes that the continuing review submission was received prior to the expiry date, and the study has been operating under the terms of the expired approval during the period of the Board's review. This is noted as an administrative matter and does not, in itself, constitute a finding of non-compliance. However, the Board wishes to clarify that the study must not enroll new participants or initiate new procedures under the expired approval.

**2. Outcome of Continuing Review**

The Board has not yet reached a decision on the continuing review submission. The submission was found to be incomplete in the following respects:

- The Continuing Review Form (CRF-2024-02) was signed by the Co-Principal Investigator rather than the Principal Investigator. The Board requires the form to be signed by the Principal Investigator.
